body: A Hard Day is a well-crafted action thriler, plenty with both cop-movie conventions and jaw-dropping twists and turns. With its efficient score and awe-inspiring cinematography, it is a pleasurable two-hour rollercoaster ride.

Lee Sun Kyun really is a world class actor. He could play as a dirty cop in this movie, then a very patient person ini My Myster, and then a cocky big boss in Parasite. A Hard Day really exploits acting skill of Sun Kyun. We could feel how depressive his situation is. The movie really centralized in Sun Kyun character. All other actors are like only supporting role. I also love the pace of this movie. For me it feels like medium pace, not too slow but not to fast either. Some parts even feels like Tarantino's style. My favorite director.

I'm an avid South Korean movie watcher. It's getting to a point where I'm seeing a least 1 per week.

There's a reason for that, they're great movies, really great movies.

The funny twist that I see on many of these police movies is that the police corruption, including the main character is considered as a norm. There is no glorifying the main character as a hero, standing above the dirty sea untarnished. He is just as dirty as the rest.

Again, a similar plot lines that runs through here is the main character is not the most likable character. Also it's more a story on a man who just happens to be a police officer rather than a police story.

These are things that have popped up quite a few times in other South Korean thrillers I've seen and it still has not gone stale.

The quirky, dirty, off beat, stylized, South Korean action movie is incredibly refreshing when placed up against the rest of the world.

This is a great movie, doesn't get into my top ten of South Korean movies but it's getting harder and harder to get into that top 10. With all the fantastic movies out there a great movie doesn't make the cut.
As my title. It's really really a hard day for the lead

Fast-paced and extremely entertaining, and that's the main thing. It's a very well-executed thriller that's consistently engaging and easy to watch, while never feeling like the kind of mindless entertainment you might feel guilty for enjoying.

Besides the ride it offers, there might not be much else to it, but that doesn't matter too much when it's this fun. Other complaints are minor- there's a very unconvincing explosion in the film's second half, and the plot might get potentially too silly and far fetched for some viewers.

It never fully jumped the shark for me, though. Yes, I could recognise the final showdown in the climax was really over the top, but it was also incredibly visceral and entertaining, much like the film as a whole.

South Korea has put out some really good action-crime-thrillers in the past decade or two, and this is among them. Pretty easy to recommend.
